column31: The logistics of doing research in space are complex, expensive, and lengthy. Scientific capabilities are limited and often times obsolete compared to Earth counterparts. Because of the changes in fundamental physics induced by weightlessness, Earth-based instruments cannot directly be adapted for space. For example, Earth’s biochemistries leverage the 1g gravity to induce sedimentation of certain chemicals; Earth liquid handlers are built to accommodate large volumes in an open environment and machines are built for large footprints. In contrast, in space — biochemistries must be re-engineerd because there is no sedimentation in microgravity; liquids must be contained; instruments must be miniaturized to be housed inside spacecraft with limited physical space. These are only a few of the many issues impacting space R&D and limiting the possibilities.
